script: [serious] In 1590, a man came home to find his entire colony gone. Including his own granddaughter. More than a hundred people. No bodies. No graves. Just one word, carved into a wooden post. Croatoan. Three years earlier, about a hundred and fifteen English settlers had landed on Roanoke Island, off what is now North Carolina. Their governor, John White, sailed back to England for supplies. He left behind his granddaughter, Virginia Dare, the first English child born in the Americas. Then England went to war with Spain, and every ship was needed against the Spanish Armada. White couldn't get back for three years. When he finally landed, in August 1590, the settlement was abandoned. The colonists had agreed on a signal. If they were forced to leave, they would carve a cross. There was no cross. Only that word. Croatoan was the name of a nearby island, and of the people who lived there. But bad weather forced White to leave before he could search it. He never found his family. Did they join the Croatoan people, or did something take them? You decide. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number twenty-seven. A new file every day.
